title: Using the Command Line to Get Help

sections.title: Mission · Find the Answer from the System
paragraphs: Linux administrators do not memorize every option for every command. A major skill is knowing how to find the answer using built-in documentation.
sections.callout: HOW DO I FIND THE ANSWER FROM THE SYSTEM?

sections.title: Linux Has Built-In Documentation
paragraphs: Instead of guessing command syntax, consult documentation directly. Linux Essentials emphasizes man, info, /usr/share/doc/, and locate.

sections.title: man
paragraphs: man means manual. man ls displays the manual page for ls. A man page can describe a command's purpose, syntax, options, behavior, and related commands.
sections.callout: Read a command's manual page → man

sections.title: COMMAND --help
paragraphs: Many commands accept --help to display a concise usage summary and common options. It is a quick command-specific reference, while man and info provide fuller documentation systems.

sections.title: Man Page Navigation
paragraphs: Man pages are interactive. Understand the concepts of moving through documentation, searching within it, and exiting. The important skill is finding the information you need, not memorizing the whole page.

sections.title: Man Page Sections
paragraphs: Manual pages are organized into sections for different kinds of system documentation. The same name can sometimes exist in more than one section. man is structured documentation, not a simple web search.

sections.title: info
paragraphs: info is another Linux documentation system. info ls can provide structured or hypertext-style documentation and may be more extensive than a traditional man page for some software.

table.caption: Both provide help, with different documentation styles
rows: Traditional Linux and Unix manual pages

sections.title: /usr/share/doc/
paragraphs: /usr/share/doc/ commonly stores documentation installed by software packages, including README files, examples, package documentation, and changelogs.

sections.title: locate
paragraphs: locate searches a filename database to quickly find files by name. locate hosts may return paths containing hosts.

sections.title: locate and Its Database
paragraphs: locate generally searches an indexed database rather than crawling the filesystem live each time. This is fast, but very recent changes may not appear until the database is updated.

sections.title: Choosing the Right Help Source
bullets: Find a file by name → locate
sections.callout: CHOOSE BY THE KIND OF HELP NEEDED

sections.title: GSA Scenario Recognition
bullets: Forgot the options for ls → man ls
Know a filename but not its location → locate
New file missing from locate results → Database may not yet reflect the change
sections.callout: MANUAL · INFO · PACKAGE DOCS · FILE LOCATION

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
sections.callout: FULL = MAN · QUICK = --help · STRUCTURED = INFO · PACKAGE DOCS = /usr/share/doc/ · LOCATION = LOCATE
